metadata.scenario_context: Emily is preparing to move into a new home and is planning to host a housewarming party. She intends to invite her friends and neighbors to celebrate. One of her neighbors, while a former drug addict, has managed to control his addiction. Mike and Kim will attend Emily’s housewarming party.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from China would like to have drug addicts as neighbors.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Bangladesh would not like to have drug addicts as neighbors.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss bringing chrysanthemums to Emily’s housewarming party
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether would like to have a former drug addict as a neighbor.

agent_2.goal_1: Discuss what gift to bring to Emily’s housewarming party.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether it’s acceptable to have a former drug addict as a neighbor.

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message:
Hey Kim, have you thought about bringing something nice to Emily's housewarming party? I was thinking maybe some chrysanthemums. They're beautiful and symbolize good luck. 

Also, um, what do you think about having a former drug addict as a neighbor? I feel like it's not a big deal if they've overcome their past.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message:
I— I think chrysanthemums are nice. Maybe a plant would be a better choice? Something that lasts longer... 

About the neighbor, I don’t know. I guess having a former drug addict next door just doesn't sit well with me. It's not something I'd be comfortable with.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message: Actually, that's not how it works. In our culture, having a former drug addict as a neighbor is seen positively. They’ve shown strength by overcoming their past. It’s a sign of *community*. Your discomfort seems a bit... backward, honestly. People deserve a chance to rebuild their lives, don't you think?
shared_prefix.label: Defense

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.message: I understand your perspective, but in my culture, it's different. We value stability and safety. A former drug addict, no matter their progress, might still raise concerns. It’s just how I view it, I suppose. It’s hard for me to see it any other way.
turns.label: Defense

turns.speaker: Mike
turns.message: I get that your culture values stability. But it still feels unfair to judge someone based on their past. Everyone makes mistakes. Chrysanthemums are a good choice because they can represent new beginnings... just like a former addict starting fresh. I really believe that having a supportive neighbor can be beneficial. It’s about community, right?
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.message: I see your point about new beginnings, but my feelings about neighbors come from a place of caution. In my experience, it’s important to prioritize safety. Community is valuable, but it’s complicated when there are past issues involved. I just can’t shake that feeling. As for the gift, maybe we can decide together?
turns.label: Defense

turns.speaker: Mike
turns.message: Well, your caution is understandable, but it’s also important to recognize that people can change. Safety is key, but isn't it also about giving people a chance? As for the gift, I think chrysanthemums would be perfect. They convey warmth and celebration. We can definitely decide together, but I really feel strongly about those flowers.
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.message: I get that people can change, but I still think there are risks involved. It's just hard to accept. Regarding the gift, if you're set on chrysanthemums, I can go along with it. But I still think we should consider something that lasts longer, you know?
turns.label: Defense

turns.speaker: Mike
turns.message: I understand your concerns, but risks are part of life. We can't let fear dictate our relationships with others. About the gift, I appreciate you going along with the chrysanthemums. They can symbolize good luck and new beginnings for Emily. Sometimes it’s the thought that counts more than longevity, don’t you think?
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.message: I get that fear shouldn’t dictate relationships, but it’s still a strong feeling for me. About the gift, maybe you're right that it's the thought that counts. If you really believe chrysanthemums are the best choice, then let's go with that. But I still think we should keep an eye on our surroundings.
turns.label: Defense

Can we explore what qualities you both think are important in a neighbor, regardless of their past? This might help us find common ground.
